lookback_notes: NOT_FOUND. The audit protocol's Area 7 states a frequency requirement for the medical reassessment (a follow-up examination occurring 6 months after the medical evaluation or upon a change in condition), but it does not state an assessor observation/look-back window in days ending on an assessment reference date. Note: an unrelated area of the same document (Area 30, Patient Review Instrument) references a 7-day look back period, which does not apply to Area 7.

federal_coding_rules.rule: The medical reassessment is a follow-up examination which occurs 6 months after the medical evaluation or upon a change in condition.

federal.criterion: A medical reassessment (follow-up examination) must be present in the record when required — 6 months after the medical evaluation or upon a change in condition; absence results in claim disallowance.

source.quote: The medical reassessment is a follow up examination which occurs 6 months after the medical evaluation or upon a change in condition. If the reassessment is missing when required, the claim will be disallowed.

federal.notes: Framed as an OMIG Audit Criteria with a stated disallowance consequence.

state_deltas.delta: New York OMIG audit criteria for the Assisted Living Program: a missing medical reassessment, required 6 months after the medical evaluation or upon a change in condition, results in disallowance of the claim. Applies to service dates 01/01/2013 through 10/31/2025.

Regulatory references cited for this audit area: 10 NYCRR § 766.6(a)(2); 18 NYCRR § 485.11(c); NYS Social Services Law § 461-L(2)(d)(iii); NYS Medicaid Program ALP Manual, Policy Guidelines Version 2006-1, Section I; for services 04/21/14 and after NYS DOH DAL 14-10; for services 04/11/14 and after NYS DOH DAL 14-09: UAS-NY FAQ.
